brief.summary_1line: After Rama departs for exile, Ayodhya falls into grief as King Dasaratha collapses in despair and denounces Kaikeyi.

image_candidates.scene_text: King Dasaratha stares down the road after Rama’s chariot until the dust disappears, then collapses to the ground in grief.
The desolate city of Ayodhya with empty markets, closed temples, and mournful citizens wandering the streets.
Dasaratha, covered in dust and supported by Kausalya while Kaikeyi stands nearby, angrily repudiates her.

deep.rich_summary: As Rama departs Ayodhya for exile, the natural world itself seems to mourn: the sky darkens, winds rage, and an earthquake shakes the city. The people of Ayodhya fall into collective grief—no one eats, joy disappears, and even family bonds seem numb with sorrow. King Dasaratha watches Rama’s chariot until the last trace of dust vanishes, then collapses in despair. When Kaikeyi approaches, he repudiates her for the demand that caused Rama’s exile, renouncing their marriage vows and rejecting her claim to him. Tormented by images of Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana suffering in the forest, the king laments how the once-pampered prince will now sleep on the ground. Returning to a silent, deserted capital, Dasaratha enters the palace overwhelmed by grief, convinced he cannot live without Rama. The chapter emphasizes cosmic sorrow and the moral cost of Kaikeyi’s ambition.

highlight_spans.why: Cosmic omen at Rama’s departure—earthquake, darkness, and disorder signal the world reacting to the exile of a righteous prince.
Dasaratha watches the dust of Rama’s chariot until it disappears and collapses in grief—one of the most poignant father–son moments.
Dasaratha angrily repudiates Kaikeyi, renouncing their marriage vows and rejecting her after the exile of Rama.
The king imagines Rama and Sita suffering in the forest—sleeping on the ground and walking among wild beasts—deepening the emotional tragedy.
Ayodhya is described as eerily empty and lifeless after Rama’s departure, symbolizing how the kingdom’s spirit is tied to him.

top_scenes.scene_text: As Rama’s chariot leaves Ayodhya, dark clouds race across the sky and the earth trembles while the city watches in dread.
King Dasaratha staring down the road at the fading cloud of dust from Rama’s chariot before collapsing onto the ground in grief.
The desolate city of Ayodhya with empty markets and silent temples as the grieving king returns through abandoned streets.
